name: The Cistern Court
summary: A paved court round the citadel's cistern: a stone drum, its lid half drawn, a winch over it, and jars waiting to be filled.
description: A citadel on a rock lives or dies by its water, and this court is where the water is kept: a stone drum over the cistern shaft with its lid dragged half aside, a timber winch on the rim for the rope, and a bucket left beside it by whoever was last on duty. Water jars stand on a stand against the north wall, a clay basin waits on its pedestal for washing, and a trough by the south wall serves the animals. The court is paved and open to the sky, and on a still night you can hear the cistern breathing.
build: Shell: the kit's OuterBailey shell, 12.0 × 12.0 × 0.30 m slab (paved), 0.50 m ochre plaster walls 3.60 m clear, 0.45 m mud-brick capstone band, an archway 2.60 × 2.59 m centred on every wall.
Cistern head (SE): a limestone drum r 1.10 × 0.80 m at (3.60, −3.60), water r 0.85 m 0.08 m below its rim.
Lid: a stone slab 1.60 × 0.80 × 0.12 m resting on the rim's north half at (3.60, −3.00), half drawn off the shaft.
Winch: two cypress posts 0.14 × 0.14 × 1.55 m standing on the rim at x 2.60 and 4.60, a beam 2.10 m across them at 2.65 m above ground.
Bucket: cypress r 0.20 × 0.35 m on the floor at (2.20, −4.80).
Hydria stand (NW): cypress, 1.60 × 0.50 m, 0.50 m high, against the north wall at x −3.80; a water jar 0.62 m tall at each end (x −4.35, −3.25).
Basin (NE): a clay bowl r 0.45 → 0.55 × 0.20 m on a pedestal r 0.08 × 0.72 m and a gypsum foot, water in it, at (3.80, 4.20); rim at 1.30 m above ground.
Trough (SW): stone, 2.20 × 0.70 × 0.60 m against the south wall at x −3.80, water in it.
Paving: limestone flags in a 1.00 m chequer (albedo only).
sockets: Archway ×4, centred on each wall: 2.60 × 2.59 m (OuterBailey), all open
Cistern shaft: SE, open under the half-drawn lid (a drop to water)

materials.name: Limestone
materials.notes: Cistern drum, trough; the lid is vellum_dim.

gameplay: Water for IGNIS fires: the court is where a burning raid can be put out, and where guards run for buckets.
The cistern head is waist-high cover; the rest of the court is open to the sky and bright.
The open shaft under the lid is a drop (a thrown item, or a player, is gone).
